# Followup Prompt
English | 中文
> Predicts your next message in DeepSeek Harness. Press Tab to use it; it never sends by itself.
After each reply, the plugin guesses what you are most likely to say next and shows it as gray text
inside the empty composer. Press **Tab** to turn it into an editable draft, or just start typing and
y composer. Press **Tab** to turn it into an editable draft, or just start typing and it disappears.
- **Unobtrusive**: appears only when the composer is empty; failures and timeouts show nothing and n

ever raise an error.
- **You stay in control**: a prediction is only a draft. You always send it you

rself.
- **Works out of the box**: uses the current session's model by default, with no extra depend
t of the box**: uses the current session's model by default, with no extra dependencies or services.
## Contents

- Installation
- Usage
- How it works
- Configuration
- FAQ
- Upgrade and uninstall
- Development
## Installation
Requires DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0` (verified on 0.2.1-rc.2) with at least one model con
DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0` (verified on 0.2.1-rc.2) with at least one model configured.
**Harness Desktop (Windows, macOS)**

1. In the sidebar, open **Plugins** → **Add plugin**.
2. Enter `dsh-followup-prompt` as the **Packag

e name or address**. In mainland China, set **Registry** to **Mainland China mirror**.
3. Click **In
stall**, then **Enable now**, and reload the page. If you are told to restart DSH, quit Harness comp
letely and open it again.
If npm is unreachable, step 2 also accepts the full path of a `dsh-followup-prompt-<version>.tgz` do
wnloaded from Releases.
**Harness Web (Windows, macOS, Linux)**
Requires Node.js `22.19` or later and pnpm.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> [!NOTE]
> Do not install from the source directory (entering this repository's path as the package
address). A directory install cannot find the dependencies that ship with Harness, so the plugin fa
ils to load. To build locally, run `pnpm pack` in this repository and install the resulting `.tgz`.
**Verify the installation**: ask a question, wait for the reply to finish, and leave the composer em
pty. Gray prediction text appears in the composer; press Tab and the text moves into the composer **
without being sent**. If no prediction appears, see the FAQ.
## Usage
When a reply finishes and the composer is empty, the prediction appears where the placeholder would
n a reply finishes and the composer is empty, the prediction appears where the placeholder would be.
| Action | Effect |
| **Tab** | The prediction becomes a draft in the composer with the cursor at the end, ready to edit

|
| **Esc** | Closes this prediction; it does not come back for this turn |
| Start typing or compo
sing with an input method | The prediction hides; once the composer is cleared, a prediction that wa

s already generated reappears |
| Start a new turn or switch sessions | The prediction hides |
Reopening a finished session also shows the prediction for its last turn.
## How it works
**What gets sent**: your messages and the visible text of the model's replies in this session. Think
ing, tool calls, tool output, and the system prompt are left out.
**When it runs**: only when a turn has finished and you're looking at the session with an empty comp
oser. The result is kept until the next turn starts, so viewing it again isn't billed again. Interru
pted or failed turns, empty sessions, and subagent sessions are skipped.
**What it predicts**: a short reply to the model's latest message, based only on what's in the conve
rsation. When there's nothing worth sending, like a plain "OK" or "thanks", or the next message depe
nds on something only you know, such as a test result, no prediction appears. Predictions can still
be wrong, so read one before you send it.
**Cost**: every prediction is an ordinary model request billed by your provider; with providers that
support prompt caching, most of the input is billed at the cached rate. To spend less, pick a cheap
er model for predictions in the settings; to stop entirely, switch the plugin off on the Plugins pag
model for predictions in the settings; to stop entirely, switch the plugin off on the Plugins page.
**Privacy**
- Data goes only to the current session's model, or to the model you set with `provider` / `model`.

Nothing is reported to any third party.
- Predictions live in memory only. They are never written to

the session log or to disk, and are gone after a restart.
- Logs record metadata only (latency, tok

en counts, outcome), never conversation content.
- There is no server-side content moderation. Predi
ctions that look like secrets are dropped locally, and you always send a prediction yourself.
## Configuration
On the **Plugins** page, find **Followup Prompt** in the **Installed** list and click its configure
button to open the settings. Click **Save** when you're done; changes take effect right away, no res
en the settings. Click **Save** when you're done; changes take effect right away, no restart needed.
The **Model** list shows the models you have already set up in DSH, the same ones you see when switc
hing models in the composer. Pick **Session default** to use whatever model your current session is
els in the composer. Pick **Session default** to use whatever model your current session is running.
To turn the plugin off, use the switch on its row in the Plugins list.
If you are comfortable with profile patches, you can also edit this plugin's `config` directly.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> `config` in a patch is replaced as a whole, not merged. When editing by hand, write
out every field even to change one; use this package's `cordis.patch.yml` as a reference. Saving fr
om the settings page also rewrites the whole `config`.
| Field | Default | Description |
| `provider` / `model` | `''` / `''` | The model used for predictions; both must be set together. Le
ave empty to follow the current session's model. Same as the **Model** option on the settings page.

|
| `reasoningEffort` | `'low'` | One of `''`, `off`, `low`, `high`, `max`. `''` uses the model's de

fault; the session's own setting is never inherited. |
